output.entity_proposed: Health Procurement and Stockpiling Bureau (the Bureau)
output.proposal: HB No. 10732 seeks to create the Health Procurement and Stockpiling Bureau under the Department of Health (DOH) as the principal agency for DOH procurement and for the stockpiling, conservation and release of strategic and critical drugs and medicines, vaccines, devices and materials, in order to respond swiftly to public health emergencies.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure, the review should examine how the proposed Bureau fits with existing DOH units, noting that Section 5 (Organization) provides for the absorption of the DOH Procurement Service and Logistics Management Division, and whether the conversion of existing units into a bureau is consistent with the streamlining and reduction of overlapping functions authorized under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). The review should also assess the relationship of the Bureau's procurement and stockpiling functions with other bodies named in Section 8 (Industrial Collaboration Program), including the Government Procurement Policy Board, the Philippine International Trading Corporation and the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council. The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, particularly its focus on the Universal Health Care system. The measure is not among the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda items identified in the available material.
legislative_history: HB No. 10732 was filed on August 11, 2026 by Representative James "Jojo" Ang Jr.; it is pending at the filing stage, and later stages are not reflected in the available records.

HB No. 4110 and HB No. 10688, filed in the 20th Congress, contain near-identical provisions on the creation of the Bureau, the Medical Stockpiling Fund and appropriations; HB No. 10688 differs in its short title and uses the acronym HPSB.
HB No. 284, HB No. 4153 and HB No. 7247 of the 19th Congress contain closely matching provisions.
HB No. 6995 (filed June 15, 2020) and HB No. 9456 (filed May 25, 2021; pending in the committee) of the 18th Congress bear the same title; their texts were not reviewed.
No committee report, substitute bill or Senate counterpart is identified in the available material.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 10732 seeks to create the Health Procurement and Stockpiling Bureau under the DOH to provide procurement services for the DOH and to stockpile and release life-saving drugs and medicines, vaccines, devices and materials during public health emergencies. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 2 (Declaration of Policy) provides that the State shall protect public health by stockpiling essential and critical drugs, vaccines, devices and materials to address public health emergencies.
b. Section 3 (Definition of Terms) defines terms used in the Act, including countertrade and its forms such as counter purchase, product buy-back, offset and trade-for-debt swap.
c. Section 4 (Creation of a Health Procurement and Stockpiling Bureau) provides that the Bureau is created under the DOH as the principal agency for DOH procurement and for medical stockpiling.
d. Section 5 (Organization) provides that the Bureau shall absorb the DOH Procurement Service and Logistics Management Division, with its organizational structure and staffing to be determined by the Secretary of Health subject to DBM approval; no positions or salary grades are specified.
e. Section 6 (Functions and Responsibilities) provides that the Bureau shall, among others, formulate procurement plans and policies, undertake procurement under the government procurement law, identify strategic and critical items for stockpiling, maintain a buffer supply, and act as supply-chain manager for stock rotation and replenishment.
f. Section 7 (Sources) provides that items may be obtained from domestic or foreign sources, with the Bureau encouraging domestic sources, including through countertrade and industrial cooperation.
g. Section 8 (Industrial Collaboration Program) provides that the DOH shall maintain partnerships with government and non-government institutions on the procurement, management, distribution and use of stockpiled items.
h. Section 9 (Establishment of Medical Stockpiling Fund and Tax Exemptions) provides for a Medical Stockpiling Fund from donations and fund-raising, with tax exemptions and deductibility for donors, and deposit of cash receipts with the National Treasury as a special account.
i. Section 10 (Report to Congress) provides that the DOH shall submit an annual report to the House and Senate health committees on or before February 15 of each year.
j. Section 11 (Appropriations) provides that initial implementation shall be charged against the current year's DOH appropriation and thereafter included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
k. Section 12 (Implementing Rules and Regulations) provides that the Secretary of Health shall issue the implementing rules within sixty (60) days from effectivity.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 10732 may be considered alongside HB No. 4110 and HB No. 10688 of the 20th Congress, which propose near-identical measures, and HB No. 284, HB No. 4153 and HB No. 7247 of the 19th Congress, which contain closely matching provisions. The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority under the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, particularly the Universal Health Care system. The review should assess whether converting the existing DOH Procurement Service and Logistics Management Division into a bureau under Section 5 (Organization) is consistent with the streamlining objectives of the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231), the cost of the staffing modifications subject to DBM approval, the fiscal implications of the tax exemptions and special account under Section 9 (Establishment of Medical Stockpiling Fund and Tax Exemptions), and the relationship of the Bureau with the Price Negotiation Board under Section 28(b) of RA No. 11223 as referenced in Section 8 (Industrial Collaboration Program).
